summary: Orchestra Ethiopia was a performing group formed in 1963 in Addis Ababa by Egyptian-born American composer and ethnomusicologist Halim El-Dabh. It brought together up to 30 traditional instrumentalists, vocalists, and dancers from many Ethiopian regions and ethnic groups, and was described as the first ensemble of its kind because these instruments and groups had never played together before. For a time the Orchestra was in residence at the Creative Arts Centre of Haile Selassie I University, now Addis Ababa University, thanks to El-Dabh's efforts.
one_line: Orchestra Ethiopia was a 1963 Addis Ababa ensemble of up to 30 traditional Ethiopian musicians and dancers from diverse ethnic groups, founded by Halim El-Dabh.
key_facts: Orchestra Ethiopia was an Ethiopian performing group formed in 1963.
Orchestra Ethiopia was formed by the Egyptian-born American composer and ethnomusicologist Halim El-Dabh.
The group was founded in Addis Ababa.
Orchestra Ethiopia comprised up to 30 traditional instrumentalists, vocalists, and dancers.
The members came from many different Ethiopian regions and ethnic groups.
Ethnic groups represented in Orchestra Ethiopia included Amhara, Tigray-Tigrinia, Oromo, Welayta, and Gimira.
Orchestra Ethiopia was the first ensemble of its type.
Before Orchestra Ethiopia, these diverse instruments and ethnic groups had never played together.
For a time, due to El-Dabh's efforts, the Orchestra was in residence at the Creative Arts Centre of Haile Selassie I University.
Haile Selassie I University is now called Addis Ababa University.
